nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Ni(OH)2-CeO2/NF precursor
nodes.procedure: The Ni(OH)2-CeO2/NF precursor was grown on Ni foam (NF) by the hydrothermal method at 120°C for 6 h using Ce(NO3)3·6H2O, Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, NH4F, and N2H4·H2O as reactants.
nodes.source_text: First, the Ni(OH)2 CeO2/NF precursor was grown on Ni foam (NF) by the hydrothermal method at 120°C for 6 h using Ce(NO3)3·6H2O, Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, NH4F, and N2H4·H2O as reactants.

nodes.name: Nitriding pyrolysis of precursor
nodes.procedure: Ni(OH)2-CeO2/NF precursor was placed in a tube furnace and pyrolyzed at 350°C for 3 h in pure NH3 atmosphere to obtain Ni3N-CeO2/NF.
nodes.source_text: Then, Ni(OH)2-CeO2/NF precursor was placed in a tube furnace and pyrolyzed at 350°C for 3 h in pure NH3 atmosphere to obtain Ni3N-CeO2/NF.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF shows peaks matching Ni₃N (JCPDS 10-0280) and CeO₂ (JCPDS 34-0394).
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD patterns in Figure 2a show that Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF sample does include Ni₃N (JCPDS 10-0280) and CeO₂ (JCPDS 34-0394)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF shows CeO₂ F₂g peak at 460 cm⁻¹, Ni₃N characteristic peak at 545 cm⁻¹, and 621 cm⁻¹ peak indicating abundant oxygen vacancies in CeO₂; CeO₂/NF lacks obvious 621 cm⁻¹ peak.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra in Figure 2b ... The peak of 460 cm⁻¹ is F₂g pattern of triple degeneracy of CeO₂, and the characteristic peak of Ni₃N at 545 cm⁻¹ further indicates successful synthesis of Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF catalyst. Moreover, the peak at 621 cm⁻¹ is assigned to the double degeneration into longitudinal optical mode of oxide, suggesting that abundant oxygen vacancies were formed in CeO₂. On the contrary, there is no obvious peak at 621 cm⁻¹ of CeO₂/NF, meaning less oxygen vacancy in the sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF shows nanosheet morphology and nanoparticle distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2c and Figure S7, Supporting Information shows the catalyst morphology, while Figure 2d confirms the uniform distribution of nanoparticle catalysts with the diameter < 100 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF shows heterogeneous interfaces with lattice fringes of 0.321 nm for CeO₂(111) and 0.216 nm for Ni₃N(002).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM images of Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF in Figure 2e and Figure S8, Supporting Information also shows abundant heterogeneous interfaces of Ni₃N and CeO₂ crystals, where the lattice fringes of 0.321 and 0.216 nm correspond to the CeO₂ (111) and Ni₃N (002) planes.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping shows uniform distribution of Ce, O, Ni, and N elements in Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDX mapping in Figure 2f demonstrates that Ni₃N nanoparticles are in full contact with CeO₂ due to the high overlap in the mapping

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF shows Ce 3d peaks at 880-895 eV (Ce 3d₅/₂) and 895-923 eV (Ce 3d₃/₂) with Ce³⁺/Ce⁴⁺ ratio of 0.65; Ni 2p peaks at 870.9 eV (Ni 2p₁/₂), 853.2 eV (Ni 2p₃/₂) for Ni-N and 855.7 eV, 873.5 eV for oxidized Ni; O 1s shows higher oxygen vacancy proportion; N 1s peaks at 397.6 eV (N-Ni) and 399.6 eV (N-H).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) was further adopted to decipher the surface chemical states of Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF ... The high-resolution Ni 2p spectrum ... the XPS spectra of N 1s of Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF manifest two peaks at 397.6 and 399.6 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF shows symmetrical EPR signal confirming abundant oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Symmetrical electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) in Figure 3e also confirms that Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF has abundant oxygen vacancies.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman of Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF during OER shows Ni₃N peak at 545 cm⁻¹ shifting to 554 cm⁻¹ at 1.33 V vs RHE, and NiOOH peaks at 477 cm⁻¹ (e_g) and 559 cm⁻¹ (A_{1g}) at 1.38 V vs RHE with wider half-peak width indicating higher oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The in situ Raman in Figure 8a shows when the voltage was increased to 1.33 V versus RHE, the peak at 545 cm⁻¹ was gradually shifted to 554 cm⁻¹ ... two distinct peaks (477 and 559 cm⁻¹) were assigned to the e_g and A_{1g} bands of NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF has double-layer capacitance C_dl of 48.62 mF cm⁻² for HER and 26.65 mF cm⁻² for OER evaluation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The double-layer capacitances (C_dl) ... measured in the non-Faraday region by Cyclic voltammetry, was used to evaluate the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA). Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF presents a higher value of 48.62 mF cm⁻² than Ni₃N/NF (37.39 mF cm⁻²) and CeO₂/NF (17.76 mF cm⁻²) ... Figure 7d indicates that the C_dl of Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF (26.65 mF cm⁻²) is larger than Ni₃N/NF (25.95 mF cm⁻²) and CeO₂/NF (10.44 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF shows lower charge transfer resistance R_ct than Ni₃N/NF and CeO₂/NF in both HER and OER conditions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Nyquist plots in Figure 4e show that Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF has the lower R_ct value than Ni₃N/NF and CeO₂/NF ... Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is used to evaluate catalyst interfacial transfer resistance (R_ct). Ni₃N-CeO₂/NF still shows the smallest R_ct (Figure 7e).
